Joel Zimmerman aka Deadmau5 is one of the world's most respected electronic music producers of the last 10 years. In those years the mouse head wearing producer has created a lot of electronic anthems which have earned him a substantial amount of awards and nominations.

Deadmau5 has decided to release 5 years of mau5, a two disc compilation featuring definitive tracks from the producers amazing catalogue plus a bunch of new and unique remixes from a long list of mau5trap friendly artists.
W:/2016ALBUM is a throwaway series of club-dance-house nothings that carve migraines out of industrial electronics.
'2448' has the most gleefully offensive hammer to the head synth line since Robbie Williams' 'Rock DJ', with that pounding, stiflingly offensive, one-note drone of trapped celebrity wind.
Nothing goes anywhere, and yet every song is so long.
The album's highlight comes in 'Glish', which is a highlight purely because A) it's a merciful two minutes and B:) it sounds precariously close to Aphex Twin's 'Windowlicker'.
There's a population out there that loves deadmau5, and will gain hours of enjoyment from hearing these bloated, meandering electro doodles.
